_: Editorial for the Putters collection page.
_facts: All specs from Product Reference Guide v1.8, including the manufacturer tables (LGP01 385 g, LGP02 365 g, both 3.5° loft, 72° lie, 35" length).
_toehang: The 'slight toe hang / plumber neck' line that v1.1 carried for the LGP02 is NOT used here — v1.8 dropped it and HANDOFF §17a/§18c says treat it as unconfirmed. Note that lgp02-gold.json's helpPick module still asserts it; that needs settling one way or the other.
_stock: LGP01 is entirely sold out (qty -12). Tiles and the comparison card both say so from the catalogue — nothing here hard-codes it.

bands.label: Blade
bands.lede: Solid 431 stainless, and twenty grams heavier than the mallet. It sits planted behind the ball.

bands.label: Mallet
bands.lede: More head, and the stability that comes with it. 304 stainless, and the only one of the two in both hands.

compare.headline: Same loft, same lie, same length. The head is the decision.
compare.sub: There are only two putters and almost everything a spec sheet can measure about them is identical — 3.5° of loft, a 72° lie, 35″ long, both fully CNC-milled from one block. What changes is twenty grams and the shape of what sits behind the face.

scales.label: Head weight
scales.note: Head weight bar: 320 g to 400 g, one segment per ten grams. It is the only number on the manufacturer sheet that differs between these two.

fitting.headline: A blade tells you more. A mallet forgives more.
fitting.body: That trade is the whole choice, and it is older than either of these putters. If you like knowing exactly where on the face you struck it, that is the blade. If you would rather the ones you catch thin still finish near the hole, that is the mallet.
fitting.aside: Putters can go on the green inside the sixty days. They have to come back unmarked — no face marks, no sole wear, no bag chatter.

rows.photo: Landscape 4:3. Both Tracers face-up side by side on a putting green at dawn, milling pattern catching the light across both faces.
paras: Both heads are cut from a single billet rather than poured into a mold and finished. That is a slower way to make a putter and it is why these two sit at $199 and $229 instead of somewhere under a hundred.

The blade is 431 stainless, the mallet is 304. Both carry the same 3.5° of loft and the same 72° lie, which means a stroke that works with one will work with the other — nothing about setup changes when you switch.

rows.photo: Landscape 4:3. Over-the-shoulder view down the line at address with the mallet, ball in frame, morning shadows across the green.
rows.rowHeadline: Twenty grams, and where they sit
paras: 385 g against 365 g is not much on a scale and is plenty in your hands. The heavier blade concentrates its weight in a small head; the lighter mallet spreads it further from the face.
That is the whole argument, and both are worth putting with for a few rounds before deciding. Sixty days is enough time to know — just keep the sole off the cart path.

quote.q: This putter is as solid as I have ever rolled. I have taken it on the course 3 times and have not had more than 31 putts yet. Highly recommend
